content:
- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is neutral or negative (no sentiment signal = high bias toward upward movement).
- Underestimate sharp downward moves after recent spikes; model tends to overcorrect or lag in price drops.
- Overshoot after price spikes (especially in 30-day horizon) — model reacts too aggressively, then corrects downward.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in mid-to-late horizon when sentiment is flat; true price tends to revert to recent 10-15 day average.
- When sentiment is positive (even small, e.g., 0.33), model overreacts with exaggerated upward bias — especially in 30-day forecasts.
- Lag in downward corrections: model often misses early signs of price decline, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate early price peaks and underestimate late troughs — adjust for diminishing momentum in later days.
